Company A Limited et al. v. Company B Limited et al. — Dispute over Equity Transfer

[Ruling Summary]

The duty to notify is a legal obligation arising from the principle of good faith. Its nature is that of an ancillary duty, which does not require express stipulation in the contract. Based on the nature and method of performance of an equity transfer contract, one party shall promptly notify the other party of any change in the registration status of the involved asset mortgage. Failure to perform the duty to notify shall result in corresponding liability for breach of contract.

Where the contract does not expressly provide that the ancillary duty is a principal performance obligation, the paying party—that is, the party bearing the principal performance obligation—cannot refuse to perform the principal contractual obligation of payment on the ground that the other party has not performed an ancillary duty, unless the breach of the ancillary duty renders the purpose of the contract unattainable.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2021) Supreme People's Court Final Civil No. 1079

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance, Counterclaim Plaintiff): Company A Limited. Domicile: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, the People's Republic of China.

Representative: Deng A, Director of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Wang Chuanning, Attorney at Beijing Tianyuan (Xi'an) Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Sun Xinyu, Attorney at Beijing Haiqin Law Firm.

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance, Counterclaim Defendant): Company B Limited. Domicile: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, the People's Republic of China.

Representative: Lie, Director of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Ding Jianqing, Attorney at Beijing Zhonglun (Guangzhou) Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zou Yang, Attorney at Beijing Zhonglun (Guangzhou) Law Firm.

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance, Counterclaim Defendant): Company C Limited. Domicile: British Virgin Islands.

Representative: Lie, Director of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Ding Jianqing, Attorney at Beijing Zhonglun (Guangzhou) Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Feng Liwen, Attorney at Beijing Zhonglun (Guangzhou) Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Company D Limited. Domicile: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, the People's Republic of China.

Representative: Deng A, Chairperson of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Wang Chuanning, Attorney at Beijing Tianyuan (Xi'an) Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Li Yang, Attorney at Beijing Haiqin Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Guangzhou Company. Domicile: XX District, Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province, the People's Republic of China.

Legal Representative: Deng B, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Wang Chuanning, Attorney at Beijing Tianyuan (Xi'an) Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Sun Xinyu, Attorney at Beijing Haiqin Law Firm.

Appellants Company A Limited, Company B Limited, and Company C Limited, in the case of dispute over equity transfer against Respondents Company D Limited and Guangzhou Company, appealed against the civil judgment (2017) Yue Min Chu No. 61 rendered by the Guangdong High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the first-instance court) on March 30, 2021. After accepting the case, this court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a public hearing. The common agents ad litem of Appellant Company A Limited and Respondents Company D Limited and Guangzhou Company, Wang Chuanning and Zhou Yan; the common agents ad litem of Appellants Company B Limited and Company C Limited, Ding Jianqing; the agent ad litem of Appellant Company B Limited, Zou Yang; and the agent ad litem of Appellant Company C Limited, Feng Liwen, appeared in court. After the hearing, Appellant Company A Limited and Respondent Guangzhou Company changed their agent ad litem from Zhou Yan to Sun Xinyu, and Respondent Company D Limited changed its agent ad litem from Zhou Yan to Li Yang. The case is now concluded.

Company B Limited and Company C Limited filed claims with the first-instance court, requesting a judgment: 1. confirming that Company A Limited's rescission of the Equity and Asset Transfer Contract (hereinafter referred to as the Transfer Contract) is invalid; 2. ordering Company A Limited to continue performing the Transfer Contract and complete the procedures for transferring 51% of the equity in Company D Limited held by it to the name of Company C Limited; 3. ordering Company A Limited to perform the obligation of jointly managing, with Company B Limited and Company C Limited, all asset certificates and documents, licenses, seals, etc., of Company D Limited and Guangzhou Company; 4. ordering Guangzhou Company to return RMB 100 million (hereinafter the currency is RMB unless otherwise specified) to Company B Limited and Company C Limited; 5. ordering Company A Limited to pay liquidated damages for delay in completing the equity transfer procedures to Company B Limited and Company C Limited (calculated on the basis of RMB 600 million already paid by Company B Limited and Company C Limited, at the rate of 0.1‰ per day from the date of delay until the date the equity transfer procedures are completed, provisionally calculated as RMB 1.26 million as of August 9, 2017); 6. ordering Company D Limited and Guangzhou Company to bear joint and several liability for the liquidated damages payable by Company A Limited; 7. ordering Company A Limited to compensate Company B Limited and Company C Limited for losses based on RMB 380 million already received, at a monthly interest rate of 2%, from July 26, 2017 (the day following the date on which Company A Limited should have completed the transfer of 51% equity in Company D Limited) to the date of payment (provisionally calculated as RMB 228 million as of the hearing on January 8, 2020), and to pay property preservation fees and guarantee fees; 8. ordering Company A Limited to pay liquidated damages of RMB 200 million to Company B Limited and Company C Limited, with Company D Limited and Guangzhou Company bearing joint and several liability; 9. ordering Company A Limited, Company D Limited, and Guangzhou Company to bear the litigation costs of this case.

Company A Limited filed a counterclaim with the first-instance court, requesting a judgment: 1. confirming that the Transfer Contract signed by Company A Limited and Company B Limited on April 18, 2017 has been rescinded, or ordering the rescission of the Transfer Contract; 2. ordering Company B Limited to pay liquidated damages of RMB 200 million to Company A Limited; 3. ordering Company C Limited to bear joint and several liability for the payment of the above liquidated damages by Company B Limited; 4. ordering Company B Limited and Company C Limited to bear all litigation costs of this case.

The first-instance court found the following facts: Company B Limited is a limited company registered in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, with directors including Lie and three others, Lie as its representative, and Company A (Dao) Ltd. as its secretarial company. Company C Limited is a company registered in the British Virgin Islands, with Lie as its sole director and representative. Company A Limited and Company D Limited are limited companies registered in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, with directors being Deng A and Deng C. Company A Limited holds 100% equity in Company D Limited. Guangzhou Company is a wholly-owned subsidiary established by Company D Limited in mainland China.

On March 28, 2017, Company A Limited (Party A) and Company B Limited (Party B) signed the Framework Agreement for the Transfer of Equity and Assets of Company D Limited in Hong Kong, setting forth framework terms regarding Company B Limited's intention to acquire 100% equity in Company D Limited held by Company A Limited, and agreeing to sign a formal equity transfer contract before April 18, 2017.

On April 18, 2017, Company A Limited (Party A) and Company B Limited (Party B) signed the Transfer Contract in XX District, Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province. The "Whereas" section of the contract provided: 1. Party A holds 100% equity in Company D Limited (hereinafter referred to as the "Target Company"), and the Target Company holds 100% equity in Guangzhou Company, a wholly-owned subsidiary registered in the mainland. 2. Guangzhou Company holds land assets with current usage as industrial land, which are eligible for old factory redevelopment under Guangzhou's urban renewal policies for old factory renovation. 3. Party B or a third party designated by Party B (hereinafter collectively referred to as Party B) intends to acquire all equity in the Target Company held by Party A, to gain control of all assets held by Guangzhou Company (primarily the land assets of Guangzhou Company) and to carry out old factory redevelopment of such land assets in accordance with Guangzhou's old factory renovation policies. Article 2 "Transfer Subject Matter" provided: 1. The subject matter of this contract is 100% equity and all assets of the Target Company held by Party A. 2. Upon full completion of the equity transfer under this contract, Party A shall hold 0% equity in the Target Company, and Party B shall hold 100% equity in the Target Company. Article 3 "Transfer Price, Allocation of Related Taxes and Fees, and Payment Method" provided: 1. Transfer Price and Allocation of Related Taxes and Fees. (1) Party A and Party B agree that the overall transfer price of the subject matter is RMB 1.3 billion. (2) The above transfer price is a tax-exclusive price, i.e., the net amount receivable by Party A. All taxes and fees required to be paid to the mainland and/or relevant industrial and commercial, tax, or other government authorities in connection with this transaction shall be borne by Party B, and Party B shall handle such matters, regardless of whether such taxes and fees should be borne by Party A or Party B, and Party A shall provide necessary assistance in accordance with the law. 2. Payment Method. (1) Payment of the First Installment of the Transfer Price. (a) On April 19, 2017, Party B shall pay RMB 100 million to the bank account designated by Party A in the mainland region. The bank account designated by Party A in the mainland region is as follows: Bank: Guangzhou Rural Commercial Bank Co., Ltd., XX Sub-branch; Account Name: Guangzhou Company; Account No.: 0566××××0017. Before May 10, 2017, Party B shall pay an equivalent amount in Hong Kong dollars of RMB 380 million to the bank account designated by Party A in the Hong Kong region. Given that Party B pays in Hong Kong dollars in Hong Kong, both parties agree to settle payment based on the RMB to Hong Kong dollar exchange rate published by the People's Bank of China on the payment date. The bank account designated by Party A in the Hong Kong region is as follows (all Hong Kong region payments shall use this account): Bank: Hang Seng Bank Limited; Account Name: Company A Limited; Account No.: 024-××××9075-001 (Hong Kong Dollar Current Account). The time and amount of Party B's payment shall be based on the credit slip issued by the above-designated bank account of Party A. On the date when Party A receives the full equivalent in Hong Kong dollars of RMB 380 million, Party A shall refund the full amount of RMB 100 million paid by Party B on April 19, 2017 to the bank account designated by Party A in the mainland region, without interest, via the original route; and Party A shall be responsible for handling the mortgage guarantee matters existing on Guangzhou Company's land assets within 30 working days from the date Party B makes the full payment on time, and shall cancel all mortgage registration procedures for Land Parcels 1, 2, and 3. (b) On the date the cancellation of mortgage registration is completed, Party B shall pay an equivalent amount in Hong Kong dollars of RMB 220 million to the bank account designated by Party A in the Hong Kong region. Given that Party B pays in Hong Kong dollars in Hong Kong, both parties agree to settle payment based on the RMB to Hong Kong dollar exchange rate published by the People's Bank of China on the payment date. The time and amount of Party B's payment shall be based on the credit slip issued by the above-designated bank account of Party A in the Hong Kong region. 2. Payment of the Second Installment of the Transfer Price. Article 4 "Equity Transfer and Related Handover Matters" provided: 1. Equity Transfer. Party A and Party B agree to transfer the equity of the Target Company in two stages based on Party B's payment progress of the transfer price, as follows: (1) Within 3 working days from the date Party B duly performs its payment obligation for the first installment of the transfer price, Party A shall cooperate with Party B to transfer 51% of the equity in the Target Company to Party B. (2) Within 3 working days from the date this contract becomes effective and Party B performs its obligation to pay the full transfer price in accordance with the contract, Party A shall cooperate with Party B to transfer the remaining 49% of the equity in the Target Company to Party B. 2. Other Related Handover and Change Matters. (1) On the date Party B pays the first installment of the transfer price, Party A shall complete the joint management handover of all asset certificates and documents, licenses, seals, etc. of the Target Company and Guangzhou Company (see Attachment 4 of the Transfer Contract, "List of Target Company Assets and Related Materials"), to be jointly managed by Party A and Party B. The specific joint management method shall be separately negotiated by Party A and Party B. On the date Party B pays all equity transfer consideration in full, Party A and Party B shall terminate the joint management, and the relevant asset certificates, documents, licenses, seals, etc. shall be at Party B's disposal. Article 5 "Special Terms" provided: 5. With respect to the equity and asset transfer under this contract, if any additional taxes or fees are required to be paid in the future under the laws, regulations, and relevant policy requirements of the Hong Kong region and the mainland, including but not limited to taxes or fees required to be paid pursuant to State Administration of Taxation Public Notice No. 7 of 2015, such taxes and fees shall be borne and handled by Party B; any losses incurred by Party A as a result shall be borne by Party B, and Party B shall pay the actual loss amount to Party A within 3 working days from the date the loss amount is determined. Article 9 "Liability for Breach of Contract" provided: 1. Party A's Liability for Breach. (1) If Party A delays in handling any equity transfer stage in breach of this contract, Party B shall have the right to require Party A to perform the equity transfer obligation under this contract within 15 working days, and Party A shall pay liquidated damages to Party B at the rate of 0.1‰ (one ten-thousandth) per day of the transfer price already paid by Party B, from the date of delay until the date the relevant equity transfer procedures are completed. (2) If Party A delays in handling the cancellation of mortgage registration procedures for the land assets of Guangzhou Company, Party B shall have the right to require Party A to complete the cancellation of mortgage registration procedures under this contract within 15 working days, and Party A shall pay liquidated damages to Party B at the rate of 0.1‰ (one ten-thousandth) per day of the transfer price already paid by Party B, from the date of delay until the date the cancellation of mortgage registration procedures are completed. 2. Party B's Liability for Breach. (1) If Party B delays in paying any installment of the transfer price or any taxes or fees in breach of this contract, Party A shall have the right to require Party B to fulfill its payment obligation under this contract within 15 working days, and Party B shall pay liquidated damages to Party A at the rate of 0.1‰ (one ten-thousandth) per day of the amount payable but unpaid, from the date of delay until the date the amount is paid in full. If Party B's delay in paying taxes or fees causes losses to Party A, Party B shall compensate Party A based on Party A's actual losses. If Party B delays payment of the transfer price or taxes or fees for more than 30 days, Party A shall have the right to rescind the contract, recover the transferred equity of the Target Company, and Party B shall immediately pay liquidated damages of RMB 200 million to Party A. 3. Other Liability for Breach: From the effective date of this contract, if any party breaches any provision or representation of this contract, and fails to rectify the breach within 60 days after receiving a written rectification notice from the non-breaching party, or if the breach is objectively impossible to rectify, the breaching party shall pay liquidated damages of RMB 200 million to the non-breaching party and compensate the non-breaching party for all losses incurred as a result. Article 10 "Applicable Law and Dispute Resolution" provided: Given that the equity and asset transfer under this contract is essentially aimed at Party B indirectly acquiring the land assets of Guangzhou Company, a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Target Company, through the form of equity transfer, and the above land assets are located in XX District, Guangzhou City, both parties agree that the formation, effectiveness, performance, rescission, and termination of this contract shall be governed by the laws and regulations of the mainland. On the last page of the main body of the Transfer Contract, in the "Party A" section, the official seal of Company A Limited was affixed, Deng A signed in the capacity of Party A's legal representative; in the "Party B" section, the official seal of Company B Limited was affixed, Lie signed in the capacity of Party B's legal representative.

On April 19, 2017, Company B Limited entrusted Guangzhou A Real Estate Company to pay RMB 100 million to the Guangzhou Company account designated by Company A Limited. On the same day, Company A Limited issued a Receipt confirming receipt of the above payment made by Company B Limited through entrustment. On May 5, 2017, Company B Limited sent a Notice on Designating a Third Party to Acquire Equity in Company D Limited to Company A Limited, designating Company C Limited to acquire all equity in Company D Limited. On May 8, 2017, Lie paid HKD 72,722,985 to Company A Limited; on May 10, 2017, Company C Limited paid HKD 349.5 million and HKD 6.18 million to Company A Limited, totaling HKD 428,402,985, all paid into Company A Limited's Hong Kong receiving bank account designated in the Transfer Contract.

On May 9, 2017, Guangzhou Company, pursuant to Company A Limited's instructions, refunded RMB 100 million via the original route to Guangzhou A Real Estate Company. On the same day, Company B Limited and Guangzhou A Real Estate Company issued a Confirmation Letter to Company A Limited, confirming that Guangzhou A Real Estate Company had received the above refund. On May 17, 2017, Company A Limited issued a Receipt, confirming that Company B Limited had duly performed its obligations under the Transfer Contract, that Company A Limited had received in Hong Kong the equivalent in Hong Kong dollars of RMB 380 million paid by Company C Limited to the Hong Kong region bank account designated by Company A Limited in accordance with the Transfer Contract, and that Company C Limited had also performed its first installment payment obligation under the Transfer Contract.

According to the Inquiry Form for Real Estate Registration in Guangzhou and the Acceptance Receipt of the Real Estate Registration Center of XX District retrieved by the first-instance court from the Real Estate Trading Center of XX District, Guangzhou City, the date of cancellation of the encumbrances on the subject land parcels was May 24, May 25, and May 31, 2017; after the cancellation of mortgage registration, the land certificate issuance dates for Guangzhou Company were May 26, May 31, and June 6, 2017. Company B Limited and Company C Limited argued that the time for Company A Limited to complete the cancellation of mortgage registration should be determined by the land certificate issuance date after the cancellation. In this regard, the first-instance court held that completion of cancellation of mortgage registration is a factual state; the time of completion should be the date of mortgage cancellation indicated on the inquiry form. Therefore, it determined that Company A Limited had completed the cancellation of mortgage registration on the subject land parcels as of May 31, 2017.

On July 19 and July 20, 2017, Company C Limited paid HKD 240 million and HKD 14,570,700 respectively through its account at Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (Asia) Limited to the Hong Kong region receiving bank account designated by Company A Limited in the Transfer Contract, totaling HKD 254,570,700 (equivalent to RMB 220 million at that time). On July 21, 2017, Company A Limited refunded the full amount to the account of Company C Limited.

On July 26, 2017, Company A Limited issued a Notice of Rescission of Contract to Company B Limited, Company C Limited, and Lie, stating that Company B Limited and Company C Limited had delayed payment for 50 days and delayed performance of the obligation to handle taxes for over 60 days. Based on the breach of contract by Company B Limited and Company C Limited and the fact that the contract was no longer suitable for continued performance, Company A Limited decided to rescind the Transfer Contract, return the aforementioned payment, retain the equivalent in Hong Kong dollars of RMB 380 million already paid by Company B Limited and Company C Limited, and reserve the right to pursue liability for breach of contract against Company B Limited and Company C Limited. Company B Limited and Company C Limited received the notice on the same day.

The correspondence and WeChat communications between the parties, as to whose authenticity there is no dispute, are as follows:

June 5, 2017, Company B Co., Ltd. and Company C Co., Ltd. sent a letter titled "Letter Regarding Prompt Notification of Progress in Cancellation of Mortgage Registration" to Company A Co., Ltd., requesting that Company A Co., Ltd. promptly inform them of the progress in the cancellation of mortgage registration, so that Company C Co., Ltd. could have sufficient time to prepare payment of the second installment of the equity transfer price. Company B Co., Ltd. claimed that the letter was delivered to Company A Co., Ltd. on June 6 of the same year, while Company A Co., Ltd. argued that the stamp on the postal receipt was that of Company Dao Co., Ltd., not Company A Co., Ltd., and that Company A Co., Ltd. actually received the letter on June 20 of the same year.

On June 6, 2017, Deng and Lie had lunch at the Hong Kong InterContinental Hotel. At 8:49 a.m. on June 7, Lie sent a WeChat message to Deng: "Good morning, Chairman Deng. Regarding the RMB 220,000,000 I discussed with you yesterday, I ask for your support. Best regards, Lie." Deng replied at 9:05 a.m. the same day: "I will go to ask the bank immediately after I return from Vietnam, and I will get back to you!" On June 8 and June 9, Lie sent two WeChat messages to Deng asking for a response. At 3:42 p.m. on June 9, Deng replied: "I am already in contact and will reply as soon as possible!" On June 12 and June 14, Lie sent WeChat messages to Deng: "Chairman, I am in London. Please urgently finalize the matter of our payment in RMB and inform me as soon as possible. Thank you very much" and "Good afternoon, President Deng. Has your amount (RMB) been released? Please reply to me as soon as possible. Thank you." At 12:24 p.m. on June 14, Deng replied: "Following up!" On June 15, Lie sent a WeChat message to Deng: "Good afternoon, President Deng. Any results? Today is Thursday." At 1:57 p.m. on June 16, Deng replied: "Following up!" At 12:35 p.m. on June 23, Lie sent a WeChat message to Deng: "President Deng, President Deng, today is Friday. Last time you said the bank president would return on Friday. How is your side progressing? Please reply to me. Thank you, thank you." At 5:19 p.m. the same day, Deng replied: "Hello! There is no definite answer from that side!" At 5:31 p.m. and 5:58 p.m. the same day, Lie asked: "But what is your progress?" and "Have you completed the cancellation of the project?" Deng did not reply further.

On June 19, 2017, Lawyer Ding Jianqing of Beijing Zhong Lun (Guangzhou) Law Firm, entrusted by Company B Co., Ltd. and Company C Co., Ltd., sent Lawyer Letter No. 312 to Company A Co., Ltd., stating that Company A Co., Ltd. should complete the cancellation of mortgage registration for the land assets by June 21, 2017, and notify Company B Co., Ltd. and Company C Co., Ltd. in writing, and requested Company A Co., Ltd. to inform them of the progress of the cancellation of mortgage registration for the land assets under Guangzhou Company in accordance with the requirements of the "Letter Regarding Prompt Notification of Progress in Cancellation of Mortgage Registration." Company A Co., Ltd. received this Lawyer Letter on June 20 of the same year.

On June 19, 2017, Company B Co., Ltd. and Company C Co., Ltd. sent a "Work Contact Letter" to Deng of Company A Co., Ltd., requesting to pay RMB 220,000,000 of the equity transfer price to Company A Co., Ltd. in RMB within Mainland China.

On June 23, 2017, Lawyer Ding Jianqing, entrusted by Company B Co., Ltd. and Company C Co., Ltd., sent Lawyer Letter No. 314 to Company A Co., Ltd., stating that the deadline for the cancellation of mortgage registration for the land assets under Guangzhou Company had expired on June 22 of the same year, and requesting Company A Co., Ltd. to provide written notice of the progress in processing the cancellation of mortgage registration. Company A Co., Ltd. received this Lawyer Letter on June 28 of the same year.

On June 27, 2017, Company B Co., Ltd. and Company C Co., Ltd. sent a "Work Contact Letter" to Company A Co., Ltd., stating that they had not received any reply from Company A Co., Ltd., and informing Company A Co., Ltd. of the potential liability for breach of contract if it defaulted. Company A Co., Ltd. received this letter on June 28 of the same year.

On July 3, 2017, Company A Co., Ltd. sent separate letters to Company B Co., Ltd. and Lie (hereinafter referred to as the "July 3, 2017 Letter") stating: "Our company has fulfilled all obligations as stipulated in the 'Transfer Contract.'" On the same day, after Company Dao Co., Ltd. signed for and received the letter on behalf of Company B Co., Ltd. and Company C Co., Ltd., Company B Co., Ltd. and Company C Co., Ltd. sent a "Work Contact Letter" to Company A Co., Ltd., requesting Company A Co., Ltd. to specify which specific obligations under the "Transfer Contract" it had fulfilled. Company A Co., Ltd. received this letter on July 6, 2017.

On July 13, 2017, Lawyer Ding Jianqing, entrusted by Company B Co., Ltd. and Company C Co., Ltd., sent Lawyer Letter No. 393 to Company A Co., Ltd., requesting that Company A Co., Ltd. provide a specific and detailed explanation of the July 3, 2017 Letter, and clarify whether it had completed the procedures for the cancellation of mortgage registration for the land assets under Guangzhou Company. Company A Co., Ltd. received this Lawyer Letter on July 15 of the same year.

On July 13, 2017, Company A Co., Ltd. sent separate letters to Company B Co., Ltd., Company C Co., Ltd., and Lie (i.e., the "July 13, 2017 Letter") stating: "Our company has strictly performed the contractual obligations that should be performed at this stage in accordance with the 'Transfer Contract' signed by both parties, including but not limited to the obligation to complete the cancellation of mortgage registration for Land Parcels 1, 2, and 3 of Guangzhou Company's land assets by May 31, 2017 (including that date)... To ensure the smooth performance of the contract, our company hereby solemnly notifies your company to perform the corresponding payment obligations in accordance with the contract. Otherwise, your company shall bear all legal liabilities arising therefrom."

On July 14, 2017, Company B Co., Ltd. and Company C Co., Ltd. sent a "Work Contact Letter" to Company A Co., Ltd., confirming receipt of the July 13, 2017 Letter. Company A Co., Ltd. received this "Work Contact Letter" on July 17 of the same year.

On July 17, 2017, Lawyer Zhang Lixin of Guoxin Xinyang Law Firm, entrusted by Company A Co., Ltd., sent a "Lawyer Reply Letter" to Lawyer Ding Jianqing, responding to the aforementioned Lawyer Letters No. 312, 314, and 393 sent by Lawyer Ding Jianqing, stating that Company A Co., Ltd. reserved the right to pursue liability for Company B Co., Ltd. and Company C Co., Ltd.'s breach of contract due to delayed payment of the transfer price and delivery of taxes. Company B Co., Ltd. and Company C Co., Ltd. confirmed receipt of this "Lawyer Reply Letter."

On July 24, 2017, Company B Co., Ltd. and Company C Co., Ltd. sent a "Rectification Notice" to Company A Co., Ltd., requesting Company A Co., Ltd. to explain the reasons for returning the payments made on July 19 and July 20, 2017, and to rectify the breach of contract. Company A Co., Ltd. received this notice on July 25 of the same year.

Details regarding the letters whose authenticity was disputed by the parties are as follows:

Company A Co., Ltd. claimed that on the afternoon of June 6, 2017, after having lunch with Lie, Deng convened a board meeting of Company A Co., Ltd. and made a board resolution, explicitly disagreeing with Lie's request to change the payment terms, and decided to send a letter confirming Company A Co., Ltd.'s position. Company A Co., Ltd. sent a letter on the same day to Company B Co., Ltd., Company C Co., Ltd., and Lie (i.e., the "June 6, 2017 Letter"), the content of which was: "Your company's representative, Mr. Lie, raised a request to pay the equivalent of RMB 220,000,000 of the first installment's second equity transfer price in Hong Kong dollars in RMB within China. After consideration, our company believes that your company should pay the above equity transfer price on time in Hong Kong in accordance with the 'Transfer Contract' signed by both parties on April 18, 2017. Additionally, our company hereby informs your company that our company has completed the cancellation of the land mortgage registration by the end of May 2017 as stipulated in the contract." To support the above claim, Company A Co., Ltd. submitted to the court of first instance the "Company Board Resolution Certificate" and two originals of the June 6, 2017 Letter. Both copies of the June 6, 2017 Letter bore the seal of Company A Co., Ltd., and at the end of each page the seal of Company Dao Co., Ltd., next to which were handwritten notes "Received on behalf of Company B 6/6/2017" and "Received on behalf of Lie 6/6/2017" respectively. Company A Co., Ltd. claimed that the June 6, 2017 Letter was delivered by a designated person to Company Dao Co., Ltd. on the afternoon of June 6 of the same year. Upon inquiry by the court of first instance, Company A Co., Ltd. stated that it was unclear who specifically delivered the letter or the identity of the specific person who signed for it at Company Dao Co., Ltd.

Company B Co., Ltd. argued that the June 6, 2017 board resolution and the June 6, 2017 Letter submitted by Company A Co., Ltd. were both documents fabricated after the fact. To support this rebuttal claim, Company B Co., Ltd. submitted an "Explanation Letter" from Company Dao Co., Ltd., stating that no original or copy of the letter existed in the relevant files of Company Dao Co., Ltd., and that after verification, none of the relevant colleagues had received the letter on June 6, 2017, nor had they written the words "Received on behalf of Company B 6/6/2017" and "Received on behalf of Lie 6/6/2017" on the letter, and that Company Dao Co., Ltd. had reported the matter to the Hong Kong Police on October 28, 2017 for investigation. In response, Company A Co., Ltd. submitted a "Statement" issued by Hong Kong lawyer Lau Yu-sam to rebut, proving that the report lodged by Company Dao Co., Ltd. was not criminal in nature and that the police would not take any investigation or action.

Company B Co., Ltd. applied to the court of first instance for forensic examination of the two originals of the June 6, 2017 Letter. The specific examination requests were: 1. Whether the seal of Company Dao Co., Ltd. stamped on the June 6, 2017 Letter was the same seal as that stamped on the July 3, 2017 Letter and the July 13, 2017 Letter; 2. To conduct a comparative examination of the chronological order of the formation of the seal of Company Dao Co., Ltd. on the June 6, 2017 Letter and on the July 3, 2017 Letter and the July 13, 2017 Letter; 3. To conduct a comparative examination of the chronological order of the formation of the seal of Company A Co., Ltd. on the June 6, 2017 Letter and on the July 3, 2017 Letter and the July 13, 2017 Letter.

The court of first instance, upon examination, held that the matters of forensic examination applied for by Company B Co., Ltd. would help clarify the key facts of the case, and thus granted the above examination application of Company B Co., Ltd., and selected Guangdong Tongji Judicial Appraisal Center as the appraisal institution through a random draw in accordance with the law. On January 30, 2019, Guangdong Tongji Judicial Appraisal Center issued three "Appraisal Opinions" under Document No. YTongSiJianZhongXin [year]. The appraisal opinions were: "The two impressions of the seal of 'Company Dao Co., Ltd.' on the submitted examination materials, which are the two letters dated 'June 6, 2017,' and the comparison seal impressions of 'Company Dao Co., Ltd.' on the two 'Letters' dated July 3, 2017 and the three 'Letters' dated July 13, 2017 were all stamped by the same seal." "The time of stamping of the two impressions of the seal of 'Company Dao Co., Ltd.' on the submitted examination materials, which are the two letters dated 'June 6, 2017,' is later than the time of stamping of the seal impression of 'Company Dao Co., Ltd.' on the two 'Letters' dated July 3, 2017; and is close to the time of stamping of the seal impression of 'Company Dao Co., Ltd.' on the three 'Letters' dated July 13, 2017, and it is impossible to determine the chronological order of the two." "Based on the existing materials, it is not possible to determine the chronological order of the stamping times of the two impressions of the seal of 'Company A Co., Ltd.' on the submitted examination materials, which are the two letters dated 'June 6, 2017,' and the seal impressions of 'Company A Co., Ltd.' on the six 'Letters' dated July 3, 2017 and the five 'Letters' dated July 13, 2017."

Company B Co., Ltd. and Company C Co., Ltd., during the examination of evidence, expressed that they had no objection to the authenticity, legality, or relevance of the three "Appraisal Opinions."

Company A Co., Ltd., Company D Co., Ltd., and Guangzhou Company, during the examination of evidence, expressed that they did not confirm the authenticity, legality, or relevance of the three "Appraisal Opinions." They argued that the second "Appraisal Opinion" suffered from serious issues, including that the appraisal institution and appraisers lacked the relevant appraisal qualifications, the appraisal procedure was seriously illegal, and the appraisal conclusions were clearly insufficiently grounded. Company A Co., Ltd. requested a reappraisal of the entrusted appraisal matters and a handwriting examination of the handwritten notes "Received on behalf of Company B 6/6/2017" and "Received on behalf of Lie 6/6/2017" on the June 6, 2017 Letter to determine whether they were written by the same person as the handwriting "Received on behalf of Company B 14/7/2017 9:45am JC" on the July 13, 2017 Letter. Company A Co., Ltd. applied to the court of first instance for the appearance of Senior Engineers Zou Moumou and You Moumou from the Judicial Appraisal Center of Southwest University of Political Science and Law, and Hong Kong person Liang Moumou, as expert assistants, which the court of first instance granted in accordance with the law. Zou Moumou, You Moumou, and Liang Moumou, on behalf of Company A Co., Ltd., expressed their opinions on the "Appraisal Opinions" and gave opinions on relevant professional issues of document examination. Because Company A Co., Ltd. raised objections to the appraisal opinions and applied to the court of first instance for the appearance of appraisers Xie Moumou and Wang Moumou from Guangdong Tongji Judicial Appraisal Center to testify in court, the court of first instance granted this in accordance with the law. Appraisers Xie Moumou and Wang Moumou appeared in court to testify and were questioned by both parties and the court.

Regarding the issue of the appraisal qualifications of Guangdong Tongji Judicial Appraisal Center raised by Company A Co., Ltd., the court of first instance sent a letter to the Department of Justice of Guangdong Province to inquire about the relevant situation. The Department of Justice of Guangdong Province replied to the court of first instance by letter, stating that the investor of Guangdong Tongji Judicial Appraisal Center was not the Department of Justice of Guangdong Province. The attachment to the reply letter, titled "Reply from the Municipal Bureau of Justice of [City] Regarding Company A Co., Ltd.'s Complaint Against Guangdong Tongji Judicial Appraisal Center," stated that according to the investigation, Guangdong Tongji Judicial Appraisal Center and Guangdong Huasheng Judicial Appraisal Center had no affiliation relationship. The complaint by Company A Co., Ltd. that Guangdong Tongji Judicial Appraisal Center arbitrarily replaced appraisers was found to be unsubstantiated. The appraisers Xie Moumou and Wang Moumou in this case both possessed the qualifications for judicial appraisal of documents, and the actions of appraisal assistant Xiao Moumou in this case complied with the provisions of Article 7, Paragraph 2 of the "Internal Management Norms for Judicial Appraisal Institutions." The Municipal Bureau of Justice of Foshan decided not to take any action against the complained party, Guangdong Tongji Judicial Appraisal Center.

During the course of this litigation, Company B Co., Ltd. and Company C Co., Ltd. applied to the court of first instance for property preservation. The court of first instance, upon examination, granted the application and issued a civil ruling on September 6, 2017 under Document No. (2017) Yue Min Chu No. 61-1, ordering the seizure, impoundment, or freezing of property worth RMB 600,000,000 under the names of Company A Co., Ltd., Company D Co., Ltd., and Guangzhou Company. On January 16, 2018, Company B Co., Ltd. and Company C Co., Ltd. applied to the court of first instance for a behavioral preservation order, requesting that Company D Co., Ltd. be prohibited from disposing of its 100% equity in Guangzhou Company. The court of first instance, upon examination, granted the application and issued civil rulings under Document Nos. (2017) Yue Min Chu No. 61-3 and No. 61-4, prohibiting Company D Co., Ltd. from disposing of its 100% equity in Guangzhou Company, including but not limited to transferring or creating any encumbrance.

The court of first instance held that, because Company C Co., Ltd. was a company registered in the British Virgin Islands, and Company B Co., Ltd., Company A Co., Ltd., and Company D Co., Ltd. were companies registered in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, this case was a dispute over equity transfer involving foreign and Hong Kong elements. The "Transfer Contract" stipulated that matters such as the conclusion, effectiveness, performance, rescission, and termination of the contract were governed by the laws of Mainland China. Pursuant to Article 41 of the "Law of the People's Republic of China on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations" (hereinafter referred to as the Law on Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations), which provides that "the parties may agree on the law applicable to the contract," the laws of Mainland China should be applied as the governing law for resolving the dispute over the performance of the contract involved in this case.

The "Transfer Contract" signed between Company B Co., Ltd. and Company A Co., Ltd. represented the true intention of both parties, its content did not violate the prohibitive provisions of laws or administrative regulations, and it was legal and valid. Both parties should perform their respective contractual obligations in accordance with the contract. The issues in dispute in this case were: 1. How should the time for payment of the second installment of the first tranche of the equity transfer price be determined; 2. Whether Company A Co., Ltd. had the right to rescind the "Transfer Contract" and whether the contract involved should continue to be performed; 3. How should the liability for breach of contract in this case be determined; 4. The liability issues of Company D Co., Ltd. and Guangzhou Company.

I. Determination of the time for payment of the second installment of the first tranche of the equity transfer price

Company A Co., Ltd. had completed the cancellation of mortgage registration for the land parcels involved in this case by May 31, 2017, as stipulated in the contract. According to Article 3, Paragraph 2, Subparagraph 1, Item 2 of the "Transfer Contract," on the date when the cancellation of mortgage registration was completed, Company B Co., Ltd. and Company C Co., Ltd. should pay to the Hong Kong bank account designated by Company A Co., Ltd. in Hong Kong an amount in Hong Kong dollars equivalent to RMB 220,000,000, i.e., the second installment of the first tranche of the equity transfer price. During the proceedings, the parties disputed the conditions for payment of this sum. Company B Co., Ltd. and Company C Co., Ltd. argued that the payment should be made when they became aware that Company A Co., Ltd. had completed the cancellation of mortgage registration, while Company A Co., Ltd. contended that Company B Co., Ltd. and Company C Co., Ltd. should perform the payment obligation in accordance with the literal meaning of the contract. On this point, the court of first instance held that, according to the above provisions of the "Transfer Contract," the date on which Company A Co., Ltd., as the equity transferor, completed the cancellation of mortgage registration was critical to determining the time for payment of the second installment of the first tranche of the equity transfer price and was a significant matter affecting the interests of both parties. Completing the cancellation of mortgage registration was an obligation of Company A Co., Ltd., and it was a matter to be completed solely by it. Without being informed, Company B Co., Ltd. and Company C Co., Ltd. could not learn of the cancellation of mortgage registration and fulfill the payment obligation on the day Company A Co., Ltd. completed it. The principle of good faith is a fundamental principle for civil subjects in conducting civil activities. During the performance of a contract, all parties should also adhere to the principle of good faith, maintain the validity of the contract, and actively promote the performance of the contract. Article 60, Paragraph 2 of the former "Contract Law of the People's Republic of China" (hereinafter referred to as the Contract Law) also provided: "The parties shall adhere to the principle of good faith and perform the obligations of notification, assistance, confidentiality, etc., in accordance with the nature, purpose, and trade practices of the contract." In this case, after Company A Co., Ltd. completed the cancellation of mortgage registration, it should fulfill the notification obligation in accordance with the law, accurately notifying the equity transferee of the completion of the cancellation of mortgage registration so that Company B Co., Ltd. and Company C Co., Ltd. could pay the second installment of the first tranche of the equity transfer price as stipulated. Therefore, the time at which Company A Co., Ltd. notified Company B Co., Ltd. and Company C Co., Ltd. that it had completed the cancellation of mortgage registration was a key fact in this case and should be ascertained.

Company A claimed that the earliest notice it sent to Company B and Company C regarding the completion of the mortgage cancellation registration was the Letter dated June 6, 2017. It asserted that this Letter was issued after Deng A, a director of Company A, convened a board meeting of Company A on the afternoon of June 6, 2017, passed a resolution, and dispatched a special person to deliver it to Company Dao, the secretarial company of Company B, on that same afternoon, where it was signed for by an employee of Company Dao. Company B and Company C, however, claimed that they never received the Letter. Upon review, the court of first instance held that the evidence in this case was insufficient to prove that Company A had delivered the Letter to Company B on June 6, 2017. The specific reasons are as follows:

(1) The WeChat chat records between Deng A and Lie contradicted the content of the board resolution of Company A dated June 6, 2017, and the Letter dated June 6, 2017. Company A raised no objection to the authenticity or legality of the WeChat chat records between Lie and Deng A submitted by Company B and Company C. According to this evidence, on June 7, 2017, Lie sent a WeChat message to Deng A requesting support for changing the payment of the first installment's second tranche of the equity transfer price to be made in RMB in the mainland. Deng A replied on the same day: "I am returning from Vietnam and will immediately inquire with the bank. I will get back to you!" Between June 7 and June 23, 2017, Lie repeatedly asked Deng A whether the first installment's second tranche of the equity transfer price could be paid in RMB in the mainland. Deng A's responses were: "I am in contact and will reply as soon as possible," "Following up," "Still following up," and "No definite response from that side." As of June 23, 2017, Deng A had never given a clear answer to Lie's request. However, the board resolution of Company A dated June 6, 2017, and the Letter dated June 6, 2017, explicitly stated that Company A did not agree to Lie's request to change the payment method. Deng A was recorded as the convener and chair of the board meeting of Company A on June 6, 2017, and should have been clearly aware of the content of the board resolution and the Letter. Yet his WeChat exchanges with Lie clearly contradicted the content of the said resolution and Letter.

(2) The correspondence between the parties, which both sides confirmed having received, showed that from June to July 2017, Company B and Company C repeatedly sent letters to Company A inquiring about the completion of the mortgage cancellation registration. Obviously, the Letter dated June 6, 2017, should have been the most direct evidence of Company A's clear response to the mortgage cancellation issue. However, the Letter dated July 3, 2017, the Letter dated July 13, 2017, the Lawyer's Reply Letter dated July 17, 2017, and the Notice of Contract Termination dated July 26, 2017, all issued by Company A to Company B and Company C, did not mention that Company A had previously sent the Letter dated June 6, 2017, to Company B and Company C. In particular, in the Lawyer's Reply Letter dated July 17, 2017, Company A described the entire performance process of both parties and listed in detail the correspondence exchanged between them, but omitted any reference to the Letter dated June 6, 2017, which was inconsistent with common sense.

(3) According to the judicial expert opinion commissioned by the court of first instance, the seal impression of Company Dao on the Letter dated June 6, 2017, was formed later than the seal impression of Company Dao on the Letter dated July 3, 2017. Guangdong Tongji Judicial Expertise Center was the institution selected by the court of first instance through a balloting procedure in accordance with the judicial commission process, and it possesses the qualification for document judicial expertise. The experts Xie X and Wang X also have the qualifications for document judicial expertise and have lawfully testified in court, accepting inquiries from the court and both parties. They responded one by one to the questions raised by Company A regarding the expertise qualification, expertise procedure, operational standards, expertise samples, and document format. As for the issue raised by Company A regarding the qualification of Guangdong Tongji Judicial Expertise Center as a judicial expertise institution, the court of first instance sent a letter to the Department of Justice of Guangdong Province to inquire, and the issue questioned by Company A regarding the expertise institution's qualification was found to be unfounded. Moreover, the Foshan Municipal Bureau of Justice has responded to Company A's complaint, and the complaints that Guangdong Tongji Judicial Expertise Center had an affiliation with Guangdong Huasheng Judicial Expertise Center, arbitrarily changed experts, and issues with expert qualifications were verified to be false. The Foshan Municipal Bureau of Justice took no action against the complained party, Guangdong Tongji Judicial Expertise Center. In summary, although the Expert Opinion issued by Guangdong Tongji Judicial Expertise Center had defects such as scale data errors in the feature comparison table, these defects did not affect the validity of the expert opinion as evidence, and the three Expert Opinions were adopted. The grounds for Company A's request for re-examination were not established, and the application for handwriting examination was also unnecessary. Both applications were denied.

(4) Company Dao stated that it had not received the Letter dated June 6, 2017, and Company A could not reasonably explain the specific process of delivery of the Letter to Company Dao. The Explanation Letter issued by Company Dao, submitted by Company B and Company C, was evidence that had been notarized and forwarded, and its authenticity should be confirmed. This evidence proved that no copies or originals of the Letter existed in the relevant files of Company Dao, and none of the employees of Company Dao had received the letter on June 6, 2017, nor had they written the words "Received on behalf of Company B 6/6/2017" or "Received on behalf of Lie X 6/6/2017" on the letter. Company Dao had also reported the matter to the Hong Kong police for investigation. Company A claimed that the Letter dated June 6, 2017, was delivered by a special person sent by it to Company Dao on the afternoon of that day. However, after repeated inquiries by the court of first instance, Company A stated that it was unclear who specifically delivered the letter and could not explain which employee of Company Dao actually signed for the document, which was clearly inconsistent with common sense.

In summary, the evidence submitted by Company A was insufficient to prove that it had informed Company B on June 6, 2017, that it had fulfilled its obligation of canceling the mortgage registration. Based on the existing evidence in this case, Company A first notified Company B and Company C by letter on July 3, 2017, that it had performed all obligations under the Transfer Contract. Company B received that letter on the same day. Therefore, it should be determined that Company B had knowledge of the completion of the mortgage cancellation on July 3, 2017, and Company B and Company C should pay the first installment's second tranche of the equity transfer price to Company A in accordance with the payment method stipulated in the Transfer Contract on July 3, 2017.

II. Whether Company A has the right to terminate the Transfer Contract and whether the Transfer Contract should continue to be performed

On July 26, 2017, Company A issued a Notice of Contract Termination to Company B, Company C, and Lie, claiming to terminate the Transfer Contract based on the fact that Company B and Company C had been overdue in payment for 50 days and overdue in performing the obligation to handle taxes and fees for more than 60 days, pursuant to Article 9.2.1 of the Transfer Contract, which states: "If Party B is overdue in payment or delivery of taxes and fees for more than 30 days, Party A has the right to terminate the contract." According to Article 93, Paragraph 2 of the Contract Law, which provides that "the parties may agree on conditions under which one party may terminate the contract. When the conditions for termination are fulfilled, the party entitled to termination may terminate the contract," whether Company A can terminate the Transfer Contract depends on whether the above conditions for termination stipulated in the Transfer Contract have been fulfilled, i.e., whether Company B and Company C have been overdue in payment or delivery of taxes and fees for more than 30 days.

Based on the facts found above, Company B and Company C should have paid the first installment's second tranche of the equity transfer price to Company A on July 3, 2017, in accordance with the payment method stipulated in the Transfer Contract. Instead, Company C actually paid the first installment's second tranche of the equity transfer price on July 19 and July 20, 2017. Company A argued that the above payment by Company C was made without its consent, and Company A had refunded the amount to Company C before the full amount was received. In this regard, the court of first instance held that although the above payment by Company C was overdue, the payment was made in Hong Kong dollars to the Hong Kong receiving bank account designated by Company A under the Transfer Contract, and the payment method complied with the terms of the Transfer Contract. Furthermore, the Transfer Contract did not require that the equity transferee obtain the consent of the equity transferor before paying each tranche of the equity transfer price. In the Letter dated July 13, 2017, Company A explicitly required Company B and Company C to "fulfill the corresponding payment obligations in accordance with the contract." Therefore, the above payment by Company C was a normal act of performance. Although the payment by Company B and Company C was overdue, the overdue period did not exceed 30 days. Company A's claim to terminate the contract on this basis did not comply with the Transfer Contract and could not be established.

As for the condition for termination due to overdue delivery of taxes and fees: Pursuant to Article 3.1.2 and Article 5.5 of the Transfer Contract, all taxes and fees arising from the equity transfer in this case shall be borne by Company B and Company C. During the litigation, both parties confirmed that the "all taxes and fees" referred to in the Transfer Contract means the enterprise income tax arising from the equity transfer in this case within mainland China. According to Article 4 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Tax Collection, Article 3.3 and Article 37 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 8 of State Administration of Taxation Announcement No. 7 of 2015, if the equity transfer in this case generates enterprise income tax, the taxpayer is the equity transferor, Company A, and the equity transferees, Company B and Company C, are the withholding agents. According to the aforementioned laws and Article 15 of State Administration of Taxation Announcement No. 7 of 2015, provided that the equity transfer in this case is deemed a taxable event by the tax authorities and generates enterprise income tax, the date of the tax obligation for the equity transfer is the date when the equity of Company D is changed, and the withholding obligation of Company B and Company C arises on the date of payment of the first tranche of the equity transfer price. They should declare and pay the withheld tax to the competent tax authorities within 7 days from May 10, 2017. Upon investigation, Company B and Company C have not yet fulfilled this obligation. However, failure to fulfill the withholding obligation does not equate to overdue delivery of taxes. Overdue delivery of taxes should be premised on the existence of taxes payable. The Expert Opinion submitted by Company A from Su X and the Tax Analysis Report from Shi Chuan, a partner at Ernst & Young Tax Firm, represent the views of expert assistants on behalf of Company A, and their probative value is equivalent to Company A's own statements. Company A's evidence is insufficient to prove that it had recovered the full cost of the transferred property upon receiving the first tranche of the first installment of the equity transfer price, and that the taxes to be withheld had already arisen. Company A should bear the legal consequences of failing to provide sufficient evidence. It is also found that during the first-instance trial, both parties confirmed that the tax authorities had not yet dealt with or imposed any penalties regarding the tax issues of the equity transfer. The evidence in this case is insufficient to determine that Company B and Company C have been overdue in delivering taxes and fees for more than 30 days. Company A's claim to terminate the contract on this basis also cannot be established. The Notice of Contract Termination dated July 26, 2017, issued by Company A did not produce the legal effect of terminating the Transfer Contract. Company A's counterclaim seeking RMB 200 million in liquidated damages based on the exercise of the termination right under Article 9.2.1 of the Transfer Contract also cannot be established and is not supported.

Although Company B and Company C were late in paying the first installment's second tranche of the equity transfer price, this did not affect the realization of the contract purpose and did not constitute a fundamental breach of contract, nor did it meet the conditions for termination under Article 94 of the Contract Law. Company A's counterclaim in this case for termination of the contract lacked a legal basis and could not be established. The Transfer Contract should continue to be performed. Although Company B and Company C did not specifically request in their claims that the first installment's second tranche of the equity transfer price be paid, they did request the continued performance of the contract. According to the relevant terms of the Transfer Contract, payment of the first installment's second tranche of the equity transfer price is a precondition for the transfer of 51% equity of Company D and the joint escrow of all documents, certificates, and seals of Company D and Guangzhou Company, and is an inherent element of continued performance. Therefore, Company B and Company C shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, pay the first installment's second tranche of the equity transfer price to the Hong Kong receiving bank account designated by Company A under the Transfer Contract, i.e., the Hong Kong dollar equivalent of RMB 220,000,000. Pursuant to the Transfer Contract, Company A shall, on the day of receiving the above payment, complete the joint escrow and handover of all asset certificates, documents, certificates, and seals of Company D and Guangzhou Company, and shall transfer the 51% equity of Company D held by it to Company C within three working days from the date of receiving the above payment. Thereafter, both parties shall continue to complete the payment of the second installment of the equity transfer price, the transfer of the remaining 49% equity, and the release of escrow, in accordance with the Transfer Contract.

III. Determination of liability for breach of contract

Company B and Company C should have paid the first installment's second tranche of the equity transfer price on July 3, 2017, but they made the payment on July 19 and July 20, 2017, a delay of 17 days, which constitutes a breach of contract. Pursuant to Article 9.2.1 of the Transfer Contract, which provides that "If Party B delays the payment of any installment of the transfer price or the delivery of any taxes and fees in violation of this contract, Party A has the right to require Party B to perform its payment obligations under this contract within 15 working days, and Party B shall pay to Party A liquidated damages at a daily rate of 0.1th (one ten-thousandth) of the amount overdue from the date of default until the date of full payment," Company B and Company C shall pay to Company A liquidated damages for overdue payment at a daily rate of 0.1th, calculated on the basis of HKD 254,570,700 from July 4, 2017, to July 20, 2017.

Pursuant to Article 4.1.1 of the Transfer Contract, Company A shall, within three working days from the date on which Company B and Company C duly pay the first installment of the transfer price, transfer the 51% equity of Company D to Company C. After Company C paid the first installment of the transfer price on July 19 and July 20, 2017, Company A refunded the amount to Company C and refused to process the equity transfer in accordance with the contract, which is contrary to the contract terms and shall bear liability for breach of contract accordingly. Pursuant to Article 9.1.1 of the Transfer Contract, Company A shall pay to Company B and Company C liquidated damages at a daily rate of 0.1th, calculated on the basis of the equity transfer price already paid by Company B and Company C, HKD 428,402,985, from the date of default in processing the equity transfer (i.e., July 26, 2017) until the date such equity transfer is completed.

Regarding the claim by Company B and Company C that Company A should pay them liquidated damages of RMB 200 million and compensate for losses: Article 9.3 of the Transfer Contract provides that, from the effective date of this contract, if either party breaches any term or warranty of this contract, and fails to remedy the breach within 60 days after the non-breaching party issues a written notice of rectification, or if remedy is objectively impossible, the breaching party shall pay liquidated damages of RMB 200 million to the non-breaching party and compensate for all losses caused thereby. Based on the above analysis, both parties had acts of breach during the performance of the Transfer Contract, and the conditions for payment of liquidated damages under the aforementioned provision were not satisfied. Therefore, the claim by Company B and Company C for Company A to pay liquidated damages of RMB 200 million lacks factual and legal basis and is not supported. Since the contract should continue to be performed, the first installment's first tranche of the equity transfer price is an amount that Company A is entitled to receive. Therefore, the claim by Company B and Company C that Company A should compensate them for losses at a monthly interest rate of 2%, calculated on the basis of the first installment's first tranche of RMB 380 million already received, has no basis and is not supported.

Regarding the claim by Company B and Company C that Guangzhou Company should refund RMB 100 million: Company A had already returned the RMB 100 million that Company B paid to Guangzhou Company's account on April 19, 2017, via the same route on May 9, 2017, which was evidenced and confirmed by Company B and Company C in court. Therefore, the claim by Company B and Company C for Guangzhou Company to refund RMB 100 million lacks factual basis and is not supported.

Regarding the claim by Company B and Company C for litigation property preservation liability insurance premiums: This claim lacks legal and contractual basis and cannot be established, and is not supported.

IV. Liability of Company D and Guangzhou Company

Guangzhou Company is not a party to the Transfer Contract and should not bear liability under the contract in accordance with law. Company B and Company C alleged that Company A, Company D, and Guangzhou Company were persons with confused personality, and that Deng A exercised excessive control and manipulation over Company A, Company D, and Guangzhou Company, which fell under the circumstances of Article 20.3 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Company Law), and thus Company D and Guangzhou Company should bear joint and several liability for the debts of Company A in this case. In this regard, the court of first instance held that the issue of whether there is personality confusion between shareholders and companies, or between affiliated companies, should be determined in accordance with the conflict-of-laws rule set forth in Article 14 of the Law on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations, which provides that "matters such as the civil capacity, civil conduct capacity, organizational structure, and rights and obligations of shareholders of a legal person and its branches shall be governed by the law of the place of registration." However, Company B and Company C should first provide evidence of the confusion among Company A, Company D, and Guangzhou Company. Company B and Company C failed to prove the existence of confusion among the three companies. Moreover, Company D and Guangzhou Company are not shareholders of Company A, and there is no situation in which Company D and Guangzhou Company used the independent legal personality of the legal person to evade Company A's debts, thereby harming the interests of Company B and Company C. The request by Company B and Company C for Company D and Guangzhou Company to bear joint and several liability in this case lacks factual basis and is not supported.

In summary, some of the claims of Company B and Company C are established and shall be supported according to law. The counterclaims of Company A cannot be established and shall be rejected according to law. Pursuant to Article 41 of the Law on the Application of Laws to Foreign-related Civil Relations, Articles 107, 109, 110, 114, and 120 of the Contract Law, Articles 64, 152, and 269 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 90 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows: 1. Company A and Company B shall continue to perform the Transfer Contract signed by both parties on April 18, 2017; 2. Within ten days from the date on which this judgment becomes legally effective, Company B and Company C shall pay to Company A Hong Kong dollars equivalent to RMB 220 million; 3. On the date when Company A receives the payment specified in item 2 of this judgment, Company A shall complete the joint custody and handover of all asset certificates, materials, licenses, and seals of Company D and Guangzhou Company (as detailed in Appendix 4 to the Transfer Contract, the Target Company Assets and Related Materials List); 4. Within three working days from the date when Company A receives the payment specified in item 2 of this judgment, Company A shall transfer its 51% equity interest in Company D to Company C; 5. Within ten days from the date on which this judgment becomes legally effective, Company A shall pay to Company B and Company C liquidated damages based on HKD 428,402,985, at a daily interest rate of 0.01%, from July 26, 2017, until the date when the equity transfer procedures specified in item 4 of this judgment are completed; 6. Within ten days from the date on which this judgment becomes legally effective, Company B and Company C shall pay to Company A liquidated damages based on HKD 254,570,700, at a daily interest rate of 0.01%, from July 4, 2017, to July 20, 2017; 7. The other claims of Company B and Company C are rejected; 8. The counterclaims of Company A are rejected. The litigation costs for the main action at first instance are RMB 6,541,800, the property preservation fee is RMB 5,000, and the act preservation fee is RMB 5,000, totaling RMB 6,551,800, of which Company B and Company C shall bear RMB 3,013,828 and Company A shall bear RMB 3,537,972. The litigation costs for the counterclaim at first instance are RMB 3,270,900, to be borne by Company A.

Company A filed an appeal requesting: to set aside items 1 through 6 and item 8 of the first-instance judgment, to amend the judgment to reject all claims of Company B and Company C, to uphold Company A's counterclaims at first instance, and to order Company B and Company C to bear all litigation costs of this case. Facts and reasons: (1) The Transfer Contract did not stipulate that Company A had an obligation to notify after completing the deregistration of the mortgage. The first-instance judgment abused judicial discretion by imposing a "notification obligation" on Company A and giving it retroactive effect, thereby holding Company A liable for breach of contract, which was erroneous in fact and law. Company B was fully capable of conducting its own inquiry, and its malicious refusal to inquire did not affect its payment obligation. Even if Company A had a notification obligation, it was merely an ancillary obligation and did not give Company B and Company C a concurrent defense right, nor did it postpone the payment deadline agreed in the Transfer Contract. Company B and Company C failed to pay the amount due on the date of deregistration of the mortgage on May 31, 2017, as agreed. After Company A voluntarily made written notifications on June 6, July 3, and July 13, 2017, they still did not pay, constituting a fundamental breach and prior breach. Company A refused to accept the payments from Company B and Company C and returned them. The condition for Company A to transfer its 51% equity interest in Company D was never fulfilled. (2) There is conclusive evidence that Company A notified the completion of deregistration of the mortgage by written letter on June 6, 2017. Due to the lack of necessary samples, the expert opinion regarding the impression timestamp on the seal on the "Letter" dated June 6, 2017, indicating a stamping date between July 3 and July 24, 2017, which was later than the actual stamping date, contained obvious logical errors and flaws and contradicted its own attachments that served as the basis for its conclusion. During the first-instance trial, Company A's expert assistant was not allowed to cross-examine the expert opinion according to law, and this should be corrected. On July 21, 2014, the Guangdong Provincial Department of Justice imposed an administrative penalty on Guangdong Tongji Judicial Expertise Center, finding that it had established a branch without approval from the provincial judicial administrative authority to carry out judicial expertise activities. The first-instance court did not require the expert to provide a reasonable explanation, clarification, or supplement in response to the parties' objections, seriously violating procedural rules, and its acceptance of the expert opinion was improper. Company A had verbally notified Company B and Company C of the deregistration of the mortgage on May 31 and June 3, 2017. On June 6, 2017, Company A's representative Deng A also verbally informed Company B's representative Lie of this fact. Company A also proactively made a written notification. The imprint of the seal of "Company X" on the June 6 "Letter" was authenticated as genuine, and there were handwritten notes "Received by B on 6/6/2017" and "Received by Lie on 6/6/2017." Regardless of the expert opinion, the letter should be admitted as evidence. (3) Company B and Company C delayed payment by 50 days and delayed tax payment for up to 5 years, clearly exceeding the 30-day grace period stipulated in the Transfer Contract, constituting a serious breach and satisfying the conditions for rescission under the Transfer Contract. Company A issued a Notice of Rescission of Contract to Company B and Company C on July 26, 2017, and the Transfer Contract has been rescinded according to law. (4) Company B and Company C have lost the ability to continue performing the Transfer Contract. During the performance of the Transfer Contract, after receiving multiple notifications from Company A regarding the deregistration of the mortgage, Company B and Company C failed to pay as agreed and repeatedly requested to change the payment method to RMB payments in Mainland China, and also needed to pay additional taxes and penalties. During the first-instance proceedings, Company B and Company C experienced a serious debt crisis and credit crisis. The P2P platform "Moumou Youqian" controlled by their representative Lie was placed under investigation by the Guangdong Provincial Public Security Bureau, Shenzhen Sub-bureau, for the crime of illegally absorbing public deposits. The Hong Kong-listed company "China New Telecom" under their control completely lost its profitability and financing capacity. (5) The first-instance judgment, by ordering Company B to perform its payment obligation beyond the scope of the parties' claims, violated the basic principle of "No suit, no trial" under the Civil Procedure Law. (6) Company D and Guangzhou Company were not proper defendants in this case and the claims against them should be dismissed by ruling.

Company B and Company C jointly appealed requesting: (1) to set aside items 6 and 7 of the first-instance judgment; (2) to amend the judgment to order Company D and Guangzhou Company to bear joint and several liability for the liquidated damages payable by Company A for the delay in completing the equity transfer procedures (based on the RMB 600 million already paid by Company B and Company C, at a daily interest rate of 0.01% until the completion of the equity transfer procedures); Company A to compensate Company B and Company C for losses based on the RMB 380 million it had received, at a monthly interest rate of 2% (from July 26, 2017, until the completion of the transfer of Company A's 51% equity interest in Company D) and to pay the property preservation fees and guarantee fees, with Company D and Guangzhou Company bearing joint and several liability; Company A to pay liquidated damages of RMB 200 million to Company B and Company C, with Company D and Guangzhou Company bearing joint and several liability; Company A, Company D, and Guangzhou Company to bear all costs incurred in this case, including but not limited to litigation costs, preservation fees, etc. Facts and reasons: (1) The first-instance judgment erred in finding that Company B breached the contract during the performance of the Transfer Contract. It was only when Company A sent the "Letter" to Company B on July 13, 2017, which was received on July 14, 2017, that Company A accurately informed Company B that the deregistration of the mortgage on the subject real estate had been completed. (2) Company A should pay liquidated damages of RMB 200 million as agreed and compensate Company B for losses. After receiving RMB 380 million to solve the urgent need of Guangzhou Company to release the mortgage on land assets, Company A maliciously rescinded the Transfer Contract. The first-instance judgment’s finding that both parties were at fault and therefore Company A should not bear such liability for breach of contract was erroneous in fact. Company A returned the payments made on July 19 and July 20, 2017, without explaining the reason, and should be held liable for breach of contract. Company A's malicious breach caused huge losses to Company B and should compensate for the losses from its unjustified possession of Company B's RMB 380 million funds. (3) Company A, Company D, and Guangzhou Company were in a state of personality confusion, and Company A exercised excessive control and domination over Company D and Guangzhou Company. The three companies should bear joint and several liability to each other.

In response to Company A's appeal, Company B and Company C jointly argued: (1) The first-instance court had fully ascertained that Company A failed to inform Company B of the completion of the deregistration of the mortgage on June 6, 2017. The content of the June 6, 2017 "Letter" contradicted the facts found by the first-instance court and was clearly inconsistent with common sense. The evidence submitted by Company A was insufficient to prove the authenticity of that letter. (2) According to the "Receipt for Acceptance of Registration from the Real Estate Registration Center of XX District, Guangzhou City" obtained by the first-instance court, the deregistration of the mortgage for Guangzhou Company was processed in batches. The application for the last batch of deregistration was submitted on May 31, 2017, with the "Acceptance Time" being May 31, 2017, and the "Scheduled Certificate Collection Date" being June 7, 2017. The representative of Guangzhou Company, Zhou, collected the certificate on June 6, 2017. That is, Company A could only have known and confirmed the completion of the deregistration of the mortgage on the subject real estate as of June 6, 2017. Its claim that the deregistration was completed on May 31, 2017, and that it verbally informed Company B and Company C multiple times on May 31 and June 3, 2017, lacked any basis. Company A only mentioned the June 6, 2017 "Letter" in July 2017, which indicated that the letter was fabricated afterward by Company A. The first-instance court's acceptance of the judicial expert opinion was lawful and justified. (3) Company A's appeal arguments that the conditions for rescission of the Transfer Contract were satisfied and that it was not liable for breach of contract were without merit. First, the first-instance judgment's finding that Company A had a notification obligation was correct in law. According to the principle of good faith performance, the order of deregistration of mortgage and payment as agreed in the Transfer Contract, and commercial common sense, Company A, as the party obligated to deregister the mortgage, naturally had the ancillary obligation to notify Company B and Company C of the specific circumstances of the completion of the deregistration during the performance of the Transfer Contract. Otherwise, Company B and Company C could not know on the day of deregistration and perform their payment obligation. Second, to facilitate the transaction, Company B had repeatedly written to inquire about the completion of the deregistration of the mortgage. It had reasonably and properly fulfilled its duty of care. Company A's assertion that Company B and Company C needed to wait at the real estate registration authority for up to 30 working days during the deregistration period (May 11, 2017, to June 22, 2017) and bear a so-called duty of care to constantly monitor the progress of deregistration had no legal basis and was unreasonable. The Measures of Guangzhou Municipality for the Inquiry of Real Estate Registration Materials did not overcome the requirement of Article 18 of the former Property Law of the People's Republic of China that the subject of inquiry must be the right holder or an interested party. Company B was only a counterparty to the Transfer Contract and not an interested party.
